sources.title: Robert C. Ellickson (faculty profile)
sources.quote_checked: Prior to entering teaching in 1970, he worked for a Presidential commission on housing policy and then for Levitt & Sons, the homebuilding firm.

sources.title: Order without Law: How Neighbors Settle Disputes
sources.quote_checked: He demonstrates that people largely govern themselves by means of informal rules—social norms—that develop without the aid of a state or other central coordinator.

sources.title: Zoning and the Cost of Housing: Evidence from Silicon Valley, Greater New Haven, and Greater Austin
sources.quote_checked: Municipal zoning, shockingly, may be the most consequential regulatory program in the United States.

sources.title: The Vast Collateral Damage of Zoning (review of America's Frozen Neighborhoods)
sources.quote_checked: I contend that a state should preempt many of the land use choices that its local governments are now free to make.

sources.title: A Year in Books: Faculty Address Critical Questions
sources.quote_checked: Ellickson creates data sets to capture how zoning policies shape 41 localities, spread across three urban areas
